text: It is vanity to follow the desires of the flesh and be led by them, for this shall bring misery at the last. It is vanity to desire a long life, and to have little care for a good life. It is vanity to take thought only for the life which now is, and not to look forward to the things which shall be hereafter. It is vanity to love that which quickly passeth away, and not to hasten where eternal joy abideth.
note: Chasing fleeting things instead of a good life

tags.when_helps: A Christian reader questioning a life chasing pleasures that quickly pass.

core_idea: Living only for passing things is vanity

text: If it seemeth to thee that thou knowest many things, and understandest them well, know also that there are many more things which thou knowest not. Be not high-minded, but rather confess thine ignorance. Why desirest thou to lift thyself above another, when there are found many more learned and more skilled in the Scripture than thou? If thou wilt know and learn anything with profit, love to be thyself unknown and to be counted for nothing.
note: Intellectual pride; admitting what you don't know

tags.when_helps: Someone inclined to rank themselves above others for what they know.

core_idea: Admit your ignorance and love being unknown

text: That is the highest and most profitable lesson, when a man truly knoweth and judgeth lowly of himself. To account nothing of one's self, and to think always kindly and highly of others, this is great and perfect wisdom. Even shouldest thou see thy neighbor sin openly or grievously, yet thou oughtest not to reckon thyself better than he, for thou knowest not how long thou shalt keep thine integrity. All of us are weak and frail; hold thou no man more frail than thyself.
note: Judging others; feeling superior to someone who failed

tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to feel superior to a person whose faults they can see.

core_idea: Think humbly of yourself and kindly of others

text: Who is so full of hindrance and annoyance to thee as thine own undisciplined heart? A man who is good and devout arrangeth beforehand within his own heart the works which he hath to do abroad; and so is not drawn away by the desires of his evil will, but subjecteth everything to the judgment of right reason. Who hath a harder battle to fight than he who striveth for self-mastery? And this should be our endeavour, even to master self, and thus daily to grow stronger than self, and go on unto perfection.
note: Self-discipline; being your own worst obstacle

situations: a habit or addiction I can't break
tags.when_helps: Someone who sees their own impulses as their main obstacle and wants to master them.

text: All perfection hath some imperfection joined to it in this life, and all our power of sight is not without some darkness. A lowly knowledge of thyself is a surer way to God than the deep searching of man's learning. Not that learning is to be blamed, nor the taking account of anything that is good; but a good conscience and a holy life is better than all.
note: Imperfection; self-knowledge over learning

tags.when_helps: Someone troubled by their imperfection who values honest self-knowledge over learning.

text: He only is truly great, who hath great charity. He is truly great who deemeth himself small, and counteth all height of honour as nothing. He is the truly wise man, who counteth all earthly things as dung that he may win Christ. And he is the truly learned man, who doeth the will of God, and forsaketh his own will.
note: What true greatness is; ambition and status

tags.when_helps: A Christian reader reconsidering what makes a person truly great.

core_idea: True greatness is love, humility and doing God's will

text: This is great wisdom, not to be hasty in action, or stubborn in our own opinions. A part of this wisdom also is not to believe every word we hear, nor to tell others all that we hear, even though we believe it. Take counsel with a man who is wise and of a good conscience; and seek to be instructed by one better than thyself, rather than to follow thine own inventions. A good life maketh a man wise toward God, and giveth him experience in many things. The more humble a man is in himself, and the more obedient towards God, the wiser will he be in all things, and the more shall his soul be at peace.
note: Making decisions carefully; gossip; seeking good advice

tags.when_helps: Someone about to act hastily who would benefit from slowing down and seeking wise counsel.

text: Whensoever a man desireth aught above measure, immediately he becometh restless. The proud and the avaricious man are never at rest; while the poor and lowly of heart abide in the multitude of peace. The man who is not yet wholly dead to self, is soon tempted, and is overcome in small and trifling matters. It is hard for him who is weak in spirit, and still in part carnal and inclined to the pleasures of sense, to withdraw himself altogether from earthly desires. And therefore, when he withdraweth himself from these, he is often sad, and easily angered too if any oppose his will.
note: Restlessness from craving; irritability

tags.when_helps: Someone restless and irritable whose excess desire keeps unsettling them.

plain_judge.issue: Drops that the weak and carnal find withdrawing from desires hard; anger at opposition softened.

text: Vain is the life of that man who putteth his trust in men or in any created Thing. Be not ashamed to be the servant of others for the love of Jesus Christ, and to be reckoned poor in this life. Rest not upon thyself, but build thy hope in God. Do what lieth in thy power, and God will help thy good intent. Trust not in thy learning, nor in the cleverness of any that lives, but rather trust in the favour of God, who resisteth the proud and giveth grace to the humble.
note: Where to place trust and hope; doing your part

tags.when_helps: A believer let down by people who wants to rest their hope in God.

Be not lifted up because of thy strength or beauty of body, for with only a slight sickness it will fail and wither away. Be not vain of thy skilfulness or ability, lest thou displease God, from whom cometh every good gift which we have.

tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to boast of wealth, looks or skill.

text: Count not thyself better than others, lest perchance thou appear worse in the sight of God, who knoweth what is in man. Be not proud of thy good works, for God's judgments are of another sort than the judgments of man, and what pleaseth man is ofttimes displeasing to Him. If thou hast any good, believe that others have more, and so thou mayest preserve thy humility. It is no harm to thee if thou place thyself below all others; but it is great harm if thou place thyself above even one. Peace is ever with the humble man, but in the heart of the proud there is envy and continual wrath.
note: Humility versus pride, envy and anger

tags.when_helps: Someone comparing themselves favourably with others and losing peace through it.

We like talking so much because we hope by our conversations to gain some mutual comfort, and because we seek to refresh our wearied spirits by variety of thoughts. tags.when_helps: Someone who regrets what they said in company and wonders why they talk so much.

text: We may enjoy abundance of peace if we refrain from busying ourselves with the sayings and doings of others, and things which concern not ourselves. note: Patience in hard times; failing in small things

tags.when_helps: A believer in a hard season who wonders whether their faith is real.

text: One hath said, "As oft as I have gone among men, so oft have I returned less a man." This is what we often experience when we have been long time in conversation. text: He who in time of peace willeth to be oversecure shall be often found in time of war overdispirited and full of fears. text: Beware, therefore, lest thou strive too earnestly after some desire which thou hast conceived, without taking counsel of Me; lest haply it repent thee afterwards, and that displease thee which before pleased, and for which thou didst long as for a great good. text: This is what frequently throweth me backward and confoundeth me before Thee, that I am so liable to fall, so weak to resist my passions. And though their assault is not altogether according to my will, it is violent and grievous, and it altogether wearieth me to live thus daily in conflict. Herein is my infirmity made known to me, that hateful fancies always rush in far more easily than they depart.
note: Weary of inner struggle and intrusive thoughts

situations: a habit or addiction I can't break
tags.when_helps: A person wearied by a daily inner fight with passions and unwanted thoughts that keep returning.

display_text: This is what frequently throweth me backward and confoundeth me before Thee, that I am so liable to fall, so weak to resist my passions. plain: Lord, what keeps setting me back is how easily I fall and how weakly I resist my passions. Their attacks are violent, and living in daily conflict wears me out. Hateful thoughts rush in far more easily than they leave.
core_idea: Bad thoughts enter easily and leave slowly

text: Oh what a life is this, where tribulations and miseries cease not, where all things are full of snares and of enemies, for when one tribulation or temptation goeth, another cometh, yea, while the former conflict is yet raging others come more in number and unexpected.
note: Troubles piling up one after another

tags.when_helps: Someone hit by one trouble after another who wants to hear that this relentlessness is known and shared.

display_text: Oh what a life is this, where tribulations and miseries cease not, where all things are full of snares and of enemies, for when one tribulation or temptation goeth, another cometh, yea, while the former conflict is yet raging others come more in number and unexpected.
plain: What a life this is, where troubles never stop and everything is full of traps and enemies; when one trouble or temptation goes, another comes, and while one battle still rages, more arrive unexpectedly.
core_idea: In this life troubles never cease

text: O Jesus, Light of Eternal Glory, solace of the wandering soul, before Thee my mouth is without speech, and my silence speaketh to Thee. How long will my Lord delay to come unto me? Let Him come unto me, His poor and humble one, and make me glad. Let Him put forth His hand, and deliver His holy one from every snare. Come, Oh come; for without Thee shall be no joyful day or hour, for Thou art my joy, and without Thee is my table empty. I am miserable, and in a manner imprisoned and loaded with fetters, until Thou refresh me by the light of Thy presence, and give me liberty, and show Thy loving countenance.
note: Longing for God in desolation

tags.when_helps: A Christian who feels imprisoned and joyless while God seems slow to come near.

plain: A prayer to Jesus: before You I have no words, and my silence speaks. How long until You come? Come, for without You no day is joyful. I feel imprisoned until Your presence refreshes and frees me.
core_idea: Without Jesus no day is joyful

plain_judge.issue: Drops plea for deliverance from snares and "Thou art my joy".

text: Behold, here I am! Behold, I come to thee, for thou didst call Me. Thy tears and the longing of thy soul, thy humbleness and contrition of heart have inclined Me, and brought Me to thee.
note: Answered longing; tears heard

tags.when_helps: A contrite believer who has been weeping and longing for God and needs to hear that they are heard.

display_text: Behold, here I am! Behold, I come to thee, for thou didst call Me. Thy tears and the longing of thy soul, thy humbleness and contrition of heart have inclined Me, and brought Me to thee.
plain: God speaks: Here I am; I come to you because you called Me. Your tears, your longing, your humility and sorrow of heart have drawn Me to you.
core_idea: God comes to the humble who call

text: But he who hath received fewer gifts, ought not to be cast down, nor to take it amiss, nor to envy him who is richer; but rather ought he to look unto Thee, and to greatly extol Thy goodness, for Thou pourest forth Thy gifts so richly, so freely and largely, without respect of persons. All things come of Thee; therefore in all things shalt thou be praised. Thou knowest what is best to be given to each; and why this man hath less, and that more, is not for us but for Thee to understand, for unto Thee each man's deservings are fully known.
note: Envy when others have more

tags.when_helps: A believer who feels less gifted than others and is tempted to envy them.

display_text: But he who hath received fewer gifts, ought not to be cast down, nor to take it amiss, nor to envy him who is richer; but rather ought he to look unto Thee, and to greatly extol Thy goodness, for Thou pourest forth Thy gifts so richly, so freely and largely, without respect of persons. plain: Someone given fewer gifts shouldn't be downcast or envy those given more, but praise God's generous goodness, the source of everything. God knows what is best for each; why one has less and another more is His to understand.
core_idea: Don't envy others' gifts; God knows best

plain_judge.issue: Passage addressed to God ("Thee") recast as speech about God; drops God knowing each one's deserving.

text: Strive, My Son, to do another's will rather than thine own. Choose always to have less rather than more. Seek always after the lowest place, and to be subject to all. Wish always and pray that the will of God be fulfilled in thee. Behold, such a man as this entereth into the inheritance of peace and quietness.
note: Four simple habits that bring peace

tags.when_helps: A person of faith restless with wanting more and seeking a path to quiet through humility.

display_text: Strive, My Son, to do another's will rather than thine own. Choose always to have less rather than more. Seek always after the lowest place, and to be subject to all. Wish always and pray that the will of God be fulfilled in thee. Behold, such a man as this entereth into the inheritance of peace and quietness.
plain: God speaks: try to do another's will rather than your own. Always choose less rather than more, seek the lowest place, and pray that God's will be done in you. Such a person enters into peace and quiet.
core_idea: Choose less and the lowest place for peace

plain_judge.issue: Drops "be subject to all".

text: O Lord my God, be not Thou far from me, my God, haste Thee to help me, for many thoughts and great fears have risen up against me, afflicting my soul. How shall I pass through them unhurt? how shall I break through them?
note: Overwhelmed by anxious thoughts and fears

tags.when_helps: A believer flooded with fearful thoughts who wants words to cry out to God for help.

display_text: O Lord my God, be not Thou far from me, my God, haste Thee to help me, for many thoughts and great fears have risen up against me, afflicting my soul. How shall I pass through them unhurt? how shall I break through them?
plain: A prayer: Lord my God, don't stay far from me; hurry to help me, for many thoughts and great fears have risen against me and torment my soul. How will I get through them unharmed?
core_idea: A plea to God amid fears

text: Enlighten me, Blessed Jesus, with the brightness of Thy inner light, and cast forth all darkness from the habitation of my heart. Restrain my many wandering thoughts, and carry away the temptations which strive to do me hurt. Fight Thou mightily for me, and drive forth the evil beasts, so call I alluring lusts, that peace may be within Thy walls and plenteousness of praise within Thy palaces, even in my pure conscience. Command Thou the winds and the storms, say unto the sea, "Be still," say unto the stormy wind, "Hold thy peace," so shall there be a great calm.
note: Prayer for calm in a restless mind

tags.when_helps: A Christian with a stormy, wandering mind who wants a prayer for inner calm.

display_text: Enlighten me, Blessed Jesus, with the brightness of Thy inner light, and cast forth all darkness from the habitation of my heart. plain: A prayer: Jesus, light up my heart and drive out its darkness. Calm my wandering thoughts and take away harmful temptations, so my conscience may have peace. Tell the wind and sea to be still, and there will be calm.
core_idea: Ask Jesus to calm the storm within

plain_judge.issue: Drops driving out "alluring lusts" and the praise within God's palaces.

text: Draw me and deliver me from every unstable comfort of creatures, for no created thing is able to satisfy my desire and to give me comfort. Join me to Thyself by the inseparable bond of love, for Thou alone art sufficient to him that loveth Thee, and without Thee all things are vain toys.
note: Nothing worldly truly satisfies

tags.when_helps: A believer finding that worldly comforts leave them unsatisfied and longing for God.

display_text: Draw me and deliver me from every unstable comfort of creatures, for no created thing is able to satisfy my desire and to give me comfort. Join me to Thyself by the inseparable bond of love, for Thou alone art sufficient to him that loveth Thee, and without Thee all things are vain toys.
plain: A prayer: draw me away from the unstable comforts of created things, for none can satisfy me. Bind me to You with unbreakable love, since You alone are enough for whoever loves You; without You everything is empty toys.
core_idea: God alone satisfies; all else is empty

text: My Son, be not curious, nor trouble thyself with vain cares. What is that to thee? Follow thou Me. For what is it to thee whether a man be this or that, or say or do thus or thus? Thou hast no need to answer for others, but thou must give an answer for thyself. Why therefore dost thou entangle thyself?
note: Preoccupied with what others do

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone entangled in worry about what other people are doing or saying.

display_text: My Son, be not curious, nor trouble thyself with vain cares. What is that to thee? Follow thou Me. For what is it to thee whether a man be this or that, or say or do thus or thus? Thou hast no need to answer for others, but thou must give an answer for thyself. Why therefore dost thou entangle thyself?
plain: God speaks: don't be nosy or fret over useless worries. What is that to you? Follow Me. Why should it matter what someone else is, says or does? You don't answer for others, only for yourself, so why get entangled?
core_idea: You answer only for yourself

text: Trouble not thyself about the shadow of a great name, nor about the friendship of many, nor about the love of men towards thee. For these things beget distraction and great sorrows of heart.
note: Craving reputation and approval

tags.when_helps: A person preoccupied with fame, popularity or being liked, and unsettled by it.

display_text: Trouble not thyself about the shadow of a great name, nor about the friendship of many, nor about the love of men towards thee. For these things beget distraction and great sorrows of heart.
plain: Don't trouble yourself about fame, having many friends, or being loved by people. These things bring distraction and great sorrow of heart.
core_idea: Fame and popularity bring distraction and sorrow

text: All men desire peace, but all do not care for the things which belong unto true peace. My peace is with the humble and lowly in heart. Thy peace shall be in much patience.
note: Wanting peace without its conditions

tags.when_helps: Someone who wants peace but has not found it, ready to hear it lies in humility and patience.

display_text: All men desire peace, but all do not care for the things which belong unto true peace. My peace is with the humble and lowly in heart. Thy peace shall be in much patience.
plain: God speaks: everyone wants peace, but not everyone cares about what true peace requires. My peace is with the humble and lowly in heart. Your peace will lie in much patience.
core_idea: Peace belongs to the humble and patient

text: Yet never to feel any disquiet, nor to suffer any pain of heart or body, this belongeth not to the present life, but is the state of eternal rest. Therefore count not thyself to have found true peace, if thou hast felt no grief; nor that then all is well if thou hast no adversary; nor that this is perfect if all things fall out according to thy desire.
note: Peace is not the absence of pain

tags.when_helps: Someone frustrated that life still hurts, who assumed peace meant never feeling disturbed.

display_text: Yet never to feel any disquiet, nor to suffer any pain of heart or body, this belongeth not to the present life, but is the state of eternal rest. Therefore count not thyself to have found true peace, if thou hast felt no grief; nor that then all is well if thou hast no adversary; nor that this is perfect if all things fall out according to thy desire.
plain: Never feeling unease or pain belongs to eternal rest, not this life. So don't think you've found true peace just because you feel no grief, have no opponent, or everything goes your way.
core_idea: Peace is not the absence of trouble

text: Lord, this is the work of a perfect man, never to slacken his mind from attention to heavenly things, and among many cares to pass along as it were without care, not after the manner of one indifferent, but rather with the privilege of a free mind, cleaving to no creature with inordinate affection.
note: Moving through many cares with a free mind

tags.when_helps: A believer surrounded by many cares who wants to move through them with a free, unclinging mind.

display_text: Lord, this is the work of a perfect man, never to slacken his mind from attention to heavenly things, and among many cares to pass along as it were without care, not after the manner of one indifferent, but rather with the privilege of a free mind, cleaving to no creature with inordinate affection.
plain: Lord, the mark of a perfect person is to keep the mind on heavenly things and pass through many cares as if free of care, not out of indifference but with a free mind, clinging to nothing with excessive attachment.
core_idea: Pass through cares with a free mind

text: Know thou that the love of thyself is more hurtful to thee than anything in the world. According to the love and inclination which thou hast, everything more or less cleaveth to thee. If thy love be pure, sincere, well-regulated, thou shalt not be in captivity to anything. Do not covet what thou mayest not have; do not have what is able to hinder thee, and to rob thee of inward liberty.
note: Attachment and self-love as captivity

tags.when_helps: Someone whose wants keep them captive and who seeks inner freedom from them.

display_text: Know thou that the love of thyself is more hurtful to thee than anything in the world. According to the love and inclination which thou hast, everything more or less cleaveth to thee. If thy love be pure, sincere, well-regulated, thou shalt not be in captivity to anything. Do not covet what thou mayest not have; do not have what is able to hinder thee, and to rob thee of inward liberty.
plain: God speaks: self-love harms you more than anything in the world. Things cling to you as your love clings to them; pure love leaves you captive to nothing. Don't covet what you can't have or keep what robs your freedom.
core_idea: Self-love harms you more than anything

text: Why art thou consumed with vain sorrow? Why art thou wearied with superfluous cares? Stand thou by My good pleasure, and thou shalt suffer no loss. If thou seekest after this or that, and wilt be here or there, according to thine own advantage or the fulfilling of thine own pleasure, thou shalt never be in quiet, nor free from care, because in everything somewhat will be found lacking, and everywhere there will be somebody who opposeth thee.
note: Restless striving never brings quiet

tags.when_helps: A person worn out by chasing their own preferences and finding something always lacking.

display_text: Why art thou consumed with vain sorrow? Why art thou wearied with superfluous cares? Stand thou by My good pleasure, and thou shalt suffer no loss. If thou seekest after this or that, and wilt be here or there, according to thine own advantage or the fulfilling of thine own pleasure, thou shalt never be in quiet, nor free from care, because in everything somewhat will be found lacking, and everywhere there will be somebody who opposeth thee.
plain: God speaks: why wear yourself out with useless sorrow and worry? Rest in My will and you lose nothing. Chase things for your own advantage or pleasure and you will never have peace; something will always be lacking.
core_idea: Chasing your own wishes never brings peace

text: The place availeth little if the spirit of devotion is wanting; nor shall that peace stand long which is sought from abroad, if the state of thy heart is without the true foundation, that is, if it abide not in Me. Thou mayest change, but thou canst not better thyself; for when occasion ariseth and is accepted thou shalt find what thou didst fly from, yea more.
note: Running away; problems follow you

tags.when_helps: Someone hoping a move or fresh start will bring peace, who needs to hear the heart travels along.

display_text: The place availeth little if the spirit of devotion is wanting; nor shall that peace stand long which is sought from abroad, if the state of thy heart is without the true foundation, that is, if it abide not in Me. Thou mayest change, but thou canst not better thyself; for when occasion ariseth and is accepted thou shalt find what thou didst fly from, yea more.
plain: A place helps little without devotion, and peace sought outside won't last if your heart isn't grounded in God. You can change where you are, but not make yourself better that way; you'll meet what you fled, and more.
core_idea: Changing places won't change your heart

text: If thou walkest inwardly, thou wilt not weigh flying words above their value. It is no small prudence to keep silence in an evil time and to turn inwardly unto Me, and not to be troubled by human judgment.
note: Hurt by gossip or criticism

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone stung by others' judgement who is tempted to answer back rather than stay quiet.

display_text: If thou walkest inwardly, thou wilt not weigh flying words above their value. It is no small prudence to keep silence in an evil time and to turn inwardly unto Me, and not to be troubled by human judgment.
plain: God speaks: if you live inwardly, you won't give passing words more weight than they deserve. It is real wisdom to stay silent in bad times, turn inward to Me, and not be troubled by people's judgment.
core_idea: Keep silent and turn inward when judged

text: Let not thy peace depend upon the word of men; for whether they judge well or ill of thee, thou art not therefore any other man than thyself. Where is true peace or true glory? Is it not in Me? And he who seeketh not to please men, nor feareth to displease, shall enjoy abundant peace. From inordinate love and vain fear ariseth all disquietude of heart, and all distraction of the senses.
note: Peace not dependent on others' opinions

tags.when_helps: A believer whose peace rises and falls with what other people think of them.

display_text: Let not thy peace depend upon the word of men; for whether they judge well or ill of thee, thou art not therefore any other man than thyself. Where is true peace or true glory? Is it not in Me? And he who seeketh not to please men, nor feareth to displease, shall enjoy abundant peace. From inordinate love and vain fear ariseth all disquietude of heart, and all distraction of the senses.
plain: Don't let your peace depend on what people say; good or bad, their opinion doesn't change who you are. True peace is in God. Whoever neither seeks to please people nor fears displeasing them will have great peace.
core_idea: Don't let your peace depend on others' words

plain_judge.issue: Drops that disquiet of heart arises from inordinate love and vain fear.

text: Lord, now am I in tribulation, and it is not well within my heart, but I am sore vexed by the suffering which lieth upon me. And now, O dear Father, what shall I say? I am taken among the snares. Save me from this hour, but for this cause came I unto this hour, that Thou mightest be glorified when I am deeply humbled and am delivered through Thee. Let it be Thy pleasure to deliver me; for what can I do who am poor, and without Thee whither shall I go? Give patience this time also. Help me, O Lord my God, and I will not fear how much soever I be weighed down.
note: Prayer in the middle of trouble

tags.when_helps: A Christian in acute trouble who needs a prayer for patience and deliverance.

display_text: Lord, now am I in tribulation, and it is not well within my heart, but I am sore vexed by the suffering which lieth upon me. And now, O dear Father, what shall I say? core_idea: In trouble, ask God for patience

text: My Son, I the Lord am a stronghold in the day of trouble. Come unto Me, when it is not well with thee.
note: Refuge when things are not well

tags.when_helps: A believer having a bad day who needs a short invitation to turn to God.

display_text: My Son, I the Lord am a stronghold in the day of trouble. Come unto Me, when it is not well with thee.
plain: God speaks: My child, I am a stronghold when trouble comes. Come to Me when things are not well with you.
core_idea: Turn to God when things go wrong

text: This it is which chiefly hindereth heavenly consolation, that thou too slowly betakest thyself unto prayer. For before thou earnestly seekest unto Me, thou dost first seek after many means of comfort, and refresheth thyself in outward things: so it cometh to pass that all things profit thee but little until thou learn that it is I who deliver those who trust in Me; neither beside Me is there any strong help, nor profitable counsel, nor enduring remedy.
note: Seeking comfort everywhere but prayer

tags.when_helps: A believer who has been seeking comfort in everything except prayer.

display_text: This it is which chiefly hindereth heavenly consolation, that thou too slowly betakest thyself unto prayer. plain: God speaks: what most blocks comfort is being slow to pray. You first try outward comforts, which help little, until you learn that I deliver those who trust Me; apart from Me there is no strong help or lasting remedy.
core_idea: Turn to prayer first, not last

text: Stand fast and with perseverance. Be long-suffering and strong. Consolation will come unto thee in its due season. Wait for Me; yea, wait; I will come and heal thee. It is temptation which vexeth thee, and a vain fear which terrifieth thee. What doth care about future events bring thee, save sorrow upon sorrow? Sufficient for the day is the evil thereof. It is vain and useless to be disturbed or lifted up about future things which perhaps will never come.
note: Worry about the future

tags.when_helps: A person of faith tormented by worry about future events that may never come.

display_text: Stand fast and with perseverance. Be long-suffering and strong. Consolation will come unto thee in its due season. Wait for Me; yea, wait; I will come and heal thee. It is temptation which vexeth thee, and a vain fear which terrifieth thee. What doth care about future events bring thee, save sorrow upon sorrow? Sufficient for the day is the evil thereof. plain: God speaks: stand firm and persevere; comfort will come in its time. Wait for Me; I will come and heal you. What troubles you is temptation and empty fear. Worrying about the future only adds sorrow to sorrow.
core_idea: Wait patiently; don't worry about tomorrow

text: Therefore let not thy heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid. Believe in Me, and put thy trust in My mercy. When thou thinkest thyself far removed from Me, I am often the nearer. Thou oughtest not to judge according to present feeling, nor so to take or give way to any grief which befalleth thee, as if all hope of escape were taken away.
note: Feeling all is lost; setbacks

tags.when_helps: A believer who feels all is lost after a setback and needs reassurance not to judge by present feeling.

display_text: Therefore let not thy heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid. Believe in Me, and put thy trust in My mercy. When thou thinkest thyself far removed from Me, I am often the nearer. core_idea: When all seems lost, God is often near

text: Think not thyself totally abandoned, although for the time I have sent to thee some tribulation, or have even withdrawn some cherished consolation; for this is the way to the Kingdom of Heaven. And without doubt it is better for thee and for all My other servants, that ye should be proved by adversities, than that ye should have all things as ye would.
note: Feeling abandoned in hardship

tags.when_helps: A Christian who feels abandoned by God in a time of trouble.

display_text: Think not thyself totally abandoned, although for the time I have sent to thee some tribulation, or have even withdrawn some cherished consolation; for this is the way to the Kingdom of Heaven. plain: God speaks: don't think yourself abandoned when I send trouble or take away a comfort you love; this is the way to heaven. It is better for you to be tested by hardship than to get everything you want.
core_idea: Hardship is not abandonment by God

text: What is more peaceful than the single eye? And what more free than he that desireth nothing upon earth?
note: Freedom of wanting little

tags.when_helps: Someone pulled in many directions by wants, drawn to the idea of a simple, undivided heart.

display_text: What is more peaceful than the single eye? And what more free than he that desireth nothing upon earth?
plain: What is more peaceful than a single-minded heart, and who is freer than the one who wants nothing on earth?
core_idea: Wanting nothing on earth brings freedom

text: We demand, how much a man hath done; but from how much virtue he acted, is not so narrowly considered. tags.when_helps: Someone measuring themselves by looks, wealth or talent who needs to hear the heart matters more.

display_text: We demand, how much a man hath done; but from how much virtue he acted, is not so narrowly considered. core_idea: We judge by achievements; grace looks at the heart

note: Freedom through letting go

tags.when_helps: A believer enslaved by wanting more who seeks the freedom of letting go.

plain: God speaks: you can't be fully free without denying yourself. The rich, the selfish and the restless are slaves, and what isn't from God will perish. Give up everything and you find everything; give up craving and you find rest.
core_idea: Give up craving and you will find rest

plain_judge.issue: Drops "not after the things of Jesus Christ" and the call to dwell on the saying.

text: My son, thou oughtest not to be turned aside, nor immediately cast down, because thou hast heard the way of the perfect. Rather oughtest thou to be provoked to higher aims, and at the least to long after the desire thereof.

core_idea: High ideals should inspire, not discourage

text: My Son, trust not thy feeling, for that which is now will be quickly changed into somewhat else. But the wise man, and he who is truly learned in spirit, standeth above these changeable things, attentive not to what he may feel in himself, or from what quarter the wind may blow, but that the whole intent of his mind may carry him on to the due and much-desired end. For thus will he be able to remain one and the same and unshaken, the single eye of his desire being steadfastly fixed, through the manifold changes of the world, upon Me.

tags.when_helps: Someone tossed between moods who wants a steady point that does not shift with feeling.

text: My God, my all! To him that understandeth, that word sufficeth, and to repeat it often is pleasing to him that loveth it. When Thou art present all things are pleasant; when Thou art absent, all things are wearisome. Thou makest the heart to be at rest, givest it deep peace and festal joy.

core_idea: With God everything is pleasant

text: If thou seek rest in this life, how then wilt thou attain unto the rest which is eternal? Set not thyself to attain much rest, but much patience. Seek the true peace, not in earth but in heaven, not in man nor in any created thing, but in God alone.

tags.when_helps: A person of faith longing for rest who is invited to seek patience and lasting peace in God instead.

display_text: If thou seek rest in this life, how then wilt thou attain unto the rest which is eternal? Set not thyself to attain much rest, but much patience. Seek the true peace, not in earth but in heaven, not in man nor in any created thing, but in God alone.

core_idea: Seek patience, not rest; peace in God alone

text: Thinkest thou that thou shalt always have spiritual consolations at thy will? My Saints had never such, but instead thereof manifold griefs, and divers temptations, and heavy desolations. But patiently they bore themselves in all, and trusted in God more than in themselves, knowing that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us. Wouldst thou have that immediately which many have hardly attained unto after many tears and hard labours? Wait for the Lord, quit thyself like a man and be strong; be not faint-hearted, nor go aside from Me, but constantly devote thy body and soul to the glory of God. I will reward thee plenteously, I will be with thee in trouble.

tags.when_helps: A believer disappointed that spiritual comfort has not come, who needs to hear the saints struggled too.

plain_judge.issue: Drops future glory outweighing present suffering, devotion to God's glory, and the promised reward.

text: My Son, anchor thy soul firmly upon God, and fear not man's judgment, when conscience pronounceth thee pious and innocent. tags.when_helps: Someone with a clear conscience who is still shaken by other people's judgement.

display_text: My Son, anchor thy soul firmly upon God, and fear not man's judgment, when conscience pronounceth thee pious and innocent. core_idea: Anchor in God; you cannot please everyone

text: Who art thou, that thou shouldst be afraid of a man that shall die? To-day he is, and to-morrow his place is not found. Fear God and thou shalt not quail before the terrors of men. What can any man do against thee by words or deeds? He hurteth himself more than thee, nor shall he escape the judgment of God, whosoever he may be.
note: Fear of other people's power

tags.when_helps: A believer intimidated by someone powerful or hostile who needs that fear put in proportion.

display_text: Who art thou, that thou shouldst be afraid of a man that shall die? To-day he is, and to-morrow his place is not found. Fear God and thou shalt not quail before the terrors of men. What can any man do against thee by words or deeds? He hurteth himself more than thee, nor shall he escape the judgment of God, whosoever he may be.
plain: Why fear a mortal who is here today and gone tomorrow? Fear God and you won't cower before people's threats. What can anyone do to you by word or deed? He harms himself more, and won't escape God's judgment.
core_idea: Fear God, not mortal people

text: My Son, lose thyself and thou shalt find Me. Stand still without all choosing and all thought of self, and thou shalt ever be a gainer. For more grace shall be added to thee, as soon as thou resignest thyself, and so long as thou dost not turn back to take thyself again.

tags.when_helps: A Christian tired of self-focus who is drawn to surrendering their own will to God.

display_text: My Son, lose thyself and thou shalt find Me. Stand still without all choosing and all thought of self, and thou shalt ever be a gainer. For more grace shall be added to thee, as soon as thou resignest thyself, and so long as thou dost not turn back to take thyself again.
plain: God speaks: lose yourself and you will find Me. Stand still, without choosing or thinking of yourself, and you will always gain. More grace comes the moment you give yourself up, as long as you don't take yourself back.
core_idea: Lose yourself and you will find God

text: Many a time I have said unto thee, and now say again, Give thyself up, resign thyself, and thou shalt have great inward peace. Give all for all; demand nothing, ask nothing in return; stand simply and with no hesitation in Me, and thou shalt possess Me. Thou shalt have liberty of heart, and the darkness shall not overwhelm thee. For this strive thou, pray for it, long after it, that thou mayest be delivered from all possession of thyself, and nakedly follow Jesus who was made naked for thee; mayest die unto thyself and live eternally to Me. Then shall all vain fancies disappear, all evil disturbings, and superfluous cares. Then also shall immoderate fear depart from thee, and inordinate love shall die.

tags.when_helps: A believer weighed down by cares and fears who seeks peace through complete self-surrender.

core_idea: Surrender yourself and find inner peace

plain_judge.issue: Drops dying to self to live eternally to God, and following Jesus "made naked for thee".

text: O Lord, right freely I commit all things to Thee; for my planning can profit but little. Oh that I did not dwell so much on future events, but could offer myself altogether to Thy pleasures without delay.

tags.when_helps: A person of faith who dwells too much on planning and future events.

display_text: O Lord, right freely I commit all things to Thee; for my planning can profit but little. Oh that I did not dwell so much on future events, but could offer myself altogether to Thy pleasures without delay.
plain: A prayer: Lord, I gladly hand everything over to You, since my planning helps little. If only I didn't dwell so much on the future, but gave myself wholly to Your will at once.
core_idea: Hand plans to God; stop dwelling on the future

text: My Son, a man often striveth vehemently after somewhat which he desireth; but when he hath obtained it he beginneth to be of another mind, because his affections towards it are not lasting, but rather rush on from one thing to another. note: Getting what you wanted, then wanting more

tags.when_helps: Someone who got what they chased and found their desire had already moved on.

core_idea: Desires fade once fulfilled

text: Verily vain glory is an evil plague, the greatest of vanities, because it draweth us away from the true glory, and robbeth us of heavenly grace. For whilst a man pleaseth himself he displeaseth Thee; whilst he gapeth after the praises of man, he is deprived of true virtues.

tags.when_helps: A believer enjoying praise a little too much, wanting a check on vanity.

plain: Vanity is a terrible plague, the greatest of vanities, because it pulls us from true glory and robs us of God's grace. While a person pleases himself he displeases God; while he craves praise, he loses real virtue.
core_idea: Craving praise robs us of true virtue

plain_judge.issue: "Displeaseth Thee" addressed to God becomes "displeases God".

text: My Son, make it no matter of thine, if thou see others honoured and exalted, and thyself despised and humbled. Lift up thine heart to Me in heaven, and then the contempt of men upon earth will not make thee sad.

tags.when_helps: A believer who sees others honoured while they are overlooked or looked down on.

core_idea: Lift your heart above others' contempt

text: My Son, if thou set thy peace on any person because thou hast high opinion of him, and art familiar with him, thou shalt be unstable and entangled. text: Many things also thou must pass by with deaf ear, and must rather think upon those things which belong unto thy peace. text: O Lord, to what have we come? Behold a temporal loss is mourned over; for a trifling gain we labour and hurry; and spiritual loss passeth away into forgetfulness, and we rarely recover it. core_idea: We mourn small losses and forget spiritual ones

core_idea: Human help fails; hope rests in God

text: Oh, how good and peacemaking a thing it is to be silent concerning others, and not carelessly to believe all reports, nor to hand them on further; how good also to lay one's self open to few, to seek ever to have Thee as the beholder of the heart; not to be carried about with every wind of words, but to desire that all things inward and outward be done according to the good pleasure of Thy will!

display_text: Oh, how good and peacemaking a thing it is to be silent concerning others, and not carelessly to believe all reports, nor to hand them on further; how good also to lay one's self open to few, to seek ever to have Thee as the beholder of the heart; not to be carried about with every wind of words, but to desire that all things inward and outward be done according to the good pleasure of Thy will!

display_text: My Son, stand fast and believe in Me. For what are words but words? They fly through the air, but they bruise no stone. If thou are guilty, think how thou wouldst gladly amend thyself; if thou knowest nothing against thyself, consider that thou wilt gladly bear this for God's sake.

core_idea: The Lord offers rest to the weary

text: Trusting in Thy goodness and great mercy, O Lord, I draw near, the sick to the Healer, the hungering and thirsting to the Fountain of life, the poverty-stricken to the King of heaven, the servant to the Lord, the creature to the Creator, the desolate to my own gentle Comforter.
note: Approaching God in need, desolation and weakness

tags.when_helps: A believer who feels needy and desolate, drawing near to God in trust.

display_text: Trusting in Thy goodness and great mercy, O Lord, I draw near, the sick to the Healer, the hungering and thirsting to the Fountain of life, the poverty-stricken to the King of heaven, the servant to the Lord, the creature to the Creator, the desolate to my own gentle Comforter.
plain: Trusting in Your goodness and mercy, Lord, I come to You as the sick come to a healer, the hungry to a fountain, the poor to a king, the creature to its Creator, the lonely to a gentle comforter.
core_idea: Coming to God as the needy come to help

plain_judge.issue: Drops "servant to the Lord" and "Fountain of life" becomes just a fountain.

text: Give me Thyself and it sufficeth, for besides Thee no consolation availeth. Without Thee I cannot be, and without Thy visitation I have no power to live.
note: Longing for God as the only true consolation

tags.when_helps: A Christian for whom nothing else consoles and who longs only for God's presence.

display_text: Give me Thyself and it sufficeth, for besides Thee no consolation availeth. Without Thee I cannot be, and without Thy visitation I have no power to live.
plain: Speaking to God: give me Yourself and that is enough, since nothing else comforts. Without You I cannot exist, and without Your presence I have no strength to live.
core_idea: God alone is enough

text: I indeed labour in the sweat of my face, I am tormented with sorrow of heart, I am burdened with sins, I am disquieted with temptations, I am entangled and oppressed with many passions, and there is none to help me, there is none to deliver and ease me, but Thou, O Lord God, my Saviour, to whom I commit myself and all things that are mine, that Thou mayest preserve me and lead me unto life eternal.
note: Overwhelmed by sorrow and burdens, entrusting oneself to God

tags.when_helps: A believer weighed down by sorrow, sin and temptation who wants to commit everything to God.

display_text: I indeed labour in the sweat of my face, I am tormented with sorrow of heart, I am burdened with sins, I am disquieted with temptations, I am entangled and oppressed with many passions, and there is none to help me, there is none to deliver and ease me, but Thou, O Lord God, my Saviour, to whom I commit myself and all things that are mine, that Thou mayest preserve me and lead me unto life eternal.
plain: I toil, grieve, carry my sins and struggle with temptations, and no one can free me except You, Lord my Saviour. I entrust myself and all I have to You, to lead me to eternal life.
core_idea: In every burden, only God can deliver

text: What more do I require of thee than thou study to resign thyself altogether unto Me? Whatsoever thou givest besides thyself, I nothing care for, for I ask not thy gift, but thee.
note: Giving oneself wholly rather than outward gifts

tags.when_helps: A believer trying to earn God's favour through offerings rather than giving themselves.

display_text: What more do I require of thee than thou study to resign thyself altogether unto Me? Whatsoever thou givest besides thyself, I nothing care for, for I ask not thy gift, but thee.
plain: God says: all I ask is that you give yourself wholly to Me. Whatever else you give means nothing to Me, because I want you, not your gifts.
core_idea: God wants you, not your gifts

text: What can I do concerning my sins, save humbly to confess and lament them and unceasingly to beseech Thy propitiation? I beseech Thee, be propitious unto me and hear me, when I stand before Thee, O my God. All my sins displease me grievously: I will never more commit them; but I grieve for them and will grieve so long as I live, steadfastly purposing to repent me truly, and to make restitution as far as I can. Forgive, O God, forgive me my sins for Thy holy Name's sake; save my soul, which Thou hast redeemed with Thy precious blood. Behold I commit myself to Thy mercy, I resign myself to Thy hands. Deal with me according to Thy loving-kindness, not according to my wickedness and iniquity.
note: Guilt, repentance and asking for mercy

tags.when_helps: A Christian grieving their wrongdoing and wanting words to ask forgiveness and make amends.

plain_judge.issue: Drops "never more commit them" and the plea to save a soul redeemed by Christ's blood.

text: Take away, O Lord, from our hearts all suspicion, indignation, anger, and contention, and whatsoever is able to injure charity and diminish brotherly love.
note: Letting go of resentment and anger toward others

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: A believer caught in suspicion and contention with others who wants to pray for charity.

display_text: Take away, O Lord, from our hearts all suspicion, indignation, anger, and contention, and whatsoever is able to injure charity and diminish brotherly love.
plain: A prayer: Lord, take from our hearts all suspicion, resentment, anger and quarrelling, and anything that harms love between people.
core_idea: Prayer to remove what harms love

text: Do thou according to the counsel of wise men, and lay aside anxiety and scruple, because it hindereth the grace of God and destroyeth devotion of mind.
note: Letting go of anxious scrupulosity

tags.when_helps: A devout person tangled in anxious scruples about whether they are doing faith right.

display_text: Do thou according to the counsel of wise men, and lay aside anxiety and scruple, because it hindereth the grace of God and destroyeth devotion of mind.
plain: Follow the advice of wise people and put aside anxiety and over-scrupulous worry, because it blocks God's grace and destroys a devoted mind.
core_idea: Anxious scruples block grace and devotion

text: Thou, O God, art my witness that nothing is able to comfort me, no creature is able to give me rest, save Thou, O my God, whom I desire to contemplate everlastingly.
note: Restlessness that only God can satisfy

tags.when_helps: A believer who finds no creature can give them rest and longs for God.

display_text: Thou, O God, art my witness that nothing is able to comfort me, no creature is able to give me rest, save Thou, O my God, whom I desire to contemplate everlastingly.
plain: Speaking to God: You are my witness that nothing and no one can comfort me or give me rest except You, whom I long to contemplate forever.
core_idea: Only God gives true rest

text: If thou hast not devotion, but rather feelest thyself dry, be instant in prayer, cease not to groan and knock; cease not until thou prevail to obtain some crumb or drop of saving grace.
note: Spiritual dryness; persisting in prayer

tags.when_helps: A believer whose prayer feels dry, who needs encouragement to keep praying.

display_text: If thou hast not devotion, but rather feelest thyself dry, be instant in prayer, cease not to groan and knock; cease not until thou prevail to obtain some crumb or drop of saving grace.
plain: If you feel no devotion and feel spiritually dry, keep praying hard. Keep groaning and knocking until you receive even a crumb or a drop of saving grace.
core_idea: In spiritual dryness, keep praying

text: Verily Thou art my Peacemaker, in Whom is perfect peace and true rest, apart from Whom is labour and sorrow and infinite misery.
note: Seeking true rest and peace in God

tags.when_helps: A Christian who finds their peace and rest in God.

display_text: Verily Thou art my Peacemaker, in Whom is perfect peace and true rest, apart from Whom is labour and sorrow and infinite misery.
plain: Speaking to God: truly You are my peacemaker. In You is perfect peace and rest; apart from You is toil, sorrow and endless misery.
core_idea: Peace is in God; misery apart from Him

text: Thou oughtest to seek earnestly the grace of devotion, to ask it fervently, to wait for it patiently and faithfully, to receive it gratefully, to preserve it humbly, to work with it diligently, and to leave to God the time and manner of heavenly visitation until it come. Chiefly oughtest thou to humble thyself when thou feelest inwardly little or no devotion, yet not to be too much cast down, nor to grieve out of measure. God ofttimes giveth in one short moment what He hath long time denied; He sometimes giveth at the end what at the beginning of prayer He hath deferred to give.
note: Patience through spiritual dryness and unanswered prayer

tags.when_helps: A believer feeling little devotion who needs patience while waiting for God's grace.

display_text: Thou oughtest to seek earnestly the grace of devotion, to ask it fervently, to wait for it patiently and faithfully, to receive it gratefully, to preserve it humbly, to work with it diligently, and to leave to God the time and manner of heavenly visitation until it come. core_idea: Wait patiently for grace; God gives in time

plain_judge.issue: Drops asking fervently, receiving gratefully, working diligently, and grace deferred to the end of prayer.

text: O most sweet and loving Lord, whom now I devoutly desire to receive, Thou knowest my infirmity and the necessity which I suffer, in what evils and vices I lie; how often I am weighed down, tempted, disturbed, and defiled. I come unto Thee for remedy, I beseech of Thee consolation and support. I speak unto Thee who knowest all things, to whom all my secrets are open, and who alone art able perfectly to comfort and help me. Thou knowest what good thing I most stand in need of, and how poor I am in virtues.
note: Bringing weakness and need honestly before God

tags.when_helps: A Christian aware of their weakness and failings who comes to God asking for comfort.

display_text: O most sweet and loving Lord, whom now I devoutly desire to receive, Thou knowest my infirmity and the necessity which I suffer, in what evils and vices I lie; how often I am weighed down, tempted, disturbed, and defiled. core_idea: Bringing one's weakness honestly to God

plain_judge.issue: Drops the eucharistic desire to receive the Lord and poverty in virtues.

text: Blessed is the simplicity which leaveth alone the difficult paths of questionings, and followeth the plain and firm steps of God's commandments. Many have lost devotion whilst they sought to search into deeper things. Faith is required of thee, and a sincere life, not loftiness of intellect, nor deepness in the mysteries of God.
note: Overthinking faith; simplicity over intellectual questioning

tags.when_helps: A believer lost in theological questions whose simple faith has gone dry.

display_text: Blessed is the simplicity which leaveth alone the difficult paths of questionings, and followeth the plain and firm steps of God's commandments. plain: Simple faith that skips difficult questioning and follows God's commandments is blessed. Many lost their devotion by probing deeper things. God asks faith and an honest life, not great intellect or insight into His mysteries.
core_idea: Faith and honest living matter more than intellect
